subject: ISV / Consultancy co-sell flight plan & billing onboarding
messages:
From: Dan O'Neill <dan@consultly.ai>
To: olga_petrov@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Consultly x Redwood — co-sell + billing onboarding

Hi Olga / Ben,

Thanks for taking this call earlier in the week — per our notes, Consultly (we're a systems integrator that embeds LLM features into client apps) is aiming to list a bundled offering on AWS Marketplace and pursue co-sell with Redwood. We have an SOW and initial usage projections attached (Consultly_SOW_v1.pdf, usage_projection.xlsx).

High level asks:
- Align on co-sell qualification steps and expected go/no-go gating for co-sell certification.
- Confirm private offer / AWS Marketplace billing flow for a bundled SKUs approach (Consultly + Redwood runtime consumption).
- Clarify which metering signals Redwood can provide for partner-led billing reconciliation (per-tenant token usage or aggregated SKU consumption).

We're targeting a June 2027 pilot with two enterprise customers; initial expected run rate ~ $20k–$40k/mo in Redwood runtime spend (see usage_projection.xlsx). Can we get an internal owner and an intake checklist so we can start the evidence handoff?

Attached: Consultly_SOW_v1.pdf, usage_projection.xlsx

Thanks — happy to set a short intake call next week.

— Dan O'Neill
VP Partnerships, Consultly
Dan@consultly.ai | +1 415-555-0179
From: olga_petrov@redwood.ai
To: Dan O'Neill <dan@consultly.ai>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 29 Oct 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Consultly x Redwood — co-sell + billing onboarding

Dan —

Appreciate the details and the attachments. Quick reply with next steps from our side:

1) Internal owners:
   - Technical intake & evidence: me (Olga Petrov) — I will run the marketplace technical checklist and collect evidences for co-sell readiness.
   - Commercial / co-sell ops: Ben Carter — I'll loop him on billing and playbook alignment.
   - Marketplace entitlements / private offer: Vivek Kulkarni — he runs our marketplace billing & entitlement workstreams.

2) Intake checklist: could you share the partner portal account email + AWS account IDs for pilot customers? Also indicate whether Consultly wants a co-bundled SKU (one listing that bills both parties) or a sell-with arrangement (Consultly lists, Redwood is visible as a third-party runtime SKU). Those two routes have different evidence and metering requirements.

3) Evidence we'd like up front: SOC2 matrix (if you have one), a short diagram of how the product calls the Redwood runtime (networking, VPC, private link), and the projected monthly spend per pilot tenant.

I can run a short ops intake meeting for 30 minutes next Tue or Wed — propose Tue 10:00–10:30 PT. If that works I'll send a calendar invite and a short shared Google doc with the checklist.

Olga
Olga Petrov
Solution Architect, Ecosystem Partnerships | Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.ai

Date: Fri, 30 Oct 2026 08:40:00 -0700

Thanks Dan — quick note from commercial side:

- We should lock a 30–45m intake to walk the SOW and confirm billing topology. I can take ownership on the sell-with vs bundle economics once we see the pilot tenant skus and expected billing cadence.
- Two billing routes we typically use: private offer (partner/ISV lists in marketplace; Redwood is a third-party billable runtime) or co-bundled listing (single SKU; requires revenue split and marketplace metering mapping). Each has different lead times for legal and metering wiring.

If you're comfortable sharing a rough monthly spend range per pilot tenant (ballpark ok), I'll draft a quick mutual action plan that maps certification steps, legal review, and a stub revenue split assumption. I'll drop the MAP into HubSpot and paste the link in the doc we use.

Proposed intake times: Tue 10:00 PT (per Olga), or Wed 09:30 PT if that helps.

Ben

- Preferred model: Consultly prefers a co-bundled listing for the pilot (single SKU) because it simplifies procurement for enterprise buyers, but we need clarity on how Redwood can expose partner-level metering to reconcile revenue splits.
- Evidence: attaching a lightweight SOC2 summary and the usage projection spreadsheet (usage_projection.xlsx). I also pasted a draft of the commercial term we expect in DocuSign — link below.
